# Write unit tests for auto-downgrade of critical priority

## Goal
Add comprehensive unit tests covering the auto-downgrade behavior for critical priority items transitioning to terminal states.

## Test Coverage Required

Per Acceptance Criteria 4 of parent (WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9):

1. **`wl update --status completed`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
2. **`wl update --stage in_review`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
3. **`wl close`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
4. **No-op: non-critical priorities** — verify high/medium/low unchanged on terminal transition
5. **No-op: non-terminal transitions** — verify critical priority unchanged when moving between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`)

## Implementation Notes

- Tests should use the existing test infrastructure (see `tests/database.test.ts` and `tests/cli/`)
- Follow the existing test patterns for `cascadePriorityDowngrade` tests
- Tests should verify both the priority change AND the reporting output (AC3 of parent)
- Consider both JSON and human-readable output paths

### Key Files
- `tests/database.test.ts` — database layer tests
- `tests/cli/` — CLI command tests (update, close)

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (sibling timestamp symptom)
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF, WL-0MOYD0UAC003YJA3, WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW (auto re-sort features)
- Victim example: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V
data.title: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

# Interview: LLM-Assisted Question Extraction

**Headline:** When `wl interview <id>` finds no parseable questions using the deterministic parser, optionally invoke a local LLM (via the existing embedding infrastructure) to extract unanswered questions from the description in free text.

## Problem Statement

The deterministic parser (`extractClarifyingSection` + `parseQAPairs`) requires an exact section header and rigid formatting. Real work items use varied formats (e.g., `## Appendix: Clarifying questions \& answers` with `- **Q1**: "..." — Answer (user@...): "..."). As a result, zero of the 17 `needsProducerReview=true` items are currently detectable. The original audit rejected WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 stating: "The command does not reliably detect questions."

An LLM normaliser turns this hard format dependency into a soft one — it can extract questions regardless of prose format.

## Users

- **Producers** running `wl interview <id>` — they want the command to find questions even when the description doesn't follow the canonical format.
- **Developers** — they want the feature to work with local models (Ollama/Foundry), not require a cloud API key.

**User Story:** "As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the system to find questions even when they're written in natural prose, so I can answer them without manually searching the description."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the deterministic parser finds no questions, and the `--llm` flag is set (or `intelligent: true` in config), the command calls a local LLM via the existing OpenAI-compatible embedding infrastructure `src/lib/search.ts`.
2. The LLM is asked to return a JSON array of `{ question: string }` objects extracted from the description, or an empty array if none found.
3. Each extracted question is presented to the user interactively (same `createPromptLoop` readline flow) for confirmation and answer.
4. Only confirmed questions are written to the description using the **deterministic re-serialiser** (`rebuildQAPairs` / `rebuildDescription`) — never written directly from LLM output.
5. When no LLM is available (no config, network failure, timeout), the command falls back to the existing deterministic-only message with no error.
6. The LLM call is bounded: description is truncated to 8 KB, a timeout of 15 seconds is enforced.
7. Tests cover: mock client returns valid questions, mock returns empty, mock throws error, no config available, timeout.

## Configuration

Opt-in via one of:
- `--llm` CLI flag: `wl interview <id> --llm`
- Config file: `intelligent: true` under `interview` section in `.worklog/config.yaml`

## Constraints

- No new dependencies — reuse `src/lib/search.ts` embedding infrastructure (OpenAI-compatible client, config resolution, graceful degradation).
- LLM is a *text completion* client, not an embedding client — but the same provider config, base URL, model, and auth apply. We should either:
  - (a) Add a `llm.*` config section parallel to `embedding.*`
  - (b) Or reuse the same provider config (the embedder already supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- The deterministic parser remains the primary path; LLM is strictly a fallback.
- Output is interactive-only (no --json mode for LLM calls).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — New `--llm` option, LLM client invocation, user confirmation loop for extracted questions.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — Add `llm?: boolean` to `InterviewOptions`.
- `src/lib/search.ts` — Potentially add a `ChatClient` class alongside the existing `OpenAIEmbedder`, or reuse its config resolution for a completion client.
- `src/config.ts` — Add `interview.llm` or `llm.*` config schema.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — New test cases for LLM path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Model availability:** Not all setups have an LLM configured. Fallback must be silent and graceful.
- **Cost:** One completion call per invocation (~2-3 KB input) is cheap even at $0.001/call, but should be bounded.
- **Hallucination:** The mandatory user-confirmation step before writing to the description mitigates this.
- **Scope creep risk:** Users may want batch extraction across multiple items or LLM-generated answers. Track separately.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MULHNZBH001A9O1** – Tests: ChatClient injectable abstraction (blocked)
- **WL-0MQD1NPAD000O7OB** – Default config entries and child item updates (completed)
- **WL-0MLPRA0VC185TUVZ** – Item Details dialog not dismissed by esc (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alongside, already, answer (+162 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, already, answer, answers, api (+149 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, alongside, already, answer, apply (+135 more)

## Goal

Pin the `ChatClient` contract with a dependency-injected unit-test suite **before** the implementation exists, so the implementation in WL-0MUQ0VOPX0037QS7 is driven by the tests (test-first).

Parent: WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF (interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/lib/llm.test.ts` exists and covers the `ChatClient` interface contract.
- Tests inject a mock/fake chat client (or fake `fetch`); **no network calls** are made.
- Tests verify: `client.available` reports `true`/`false` correctly from configuration presence; `complete(prompt)` returns the provider's response string; the configured timeout is enforced; API/HTTP errors are surfaced as a rejected promise.
- The file runs under `npm test` and is **red** (failing) until WL-0MUQ0VOPX0037QS7 lands; after WL-0MUQ0VOPX0037QS7 it is green.
- No existing test regresses.

## Minimal Implementation

- Create `tests/lib/llm.test.ts` following the style of `tests/unit/config-llm.test.ts`.
- Define a `MockChatClient` implementing the target `ChatClient` interface, returning deterministic strings.
- Cover the five cases: available, unavailable, `complete()` success, timeout (use `vi.useFakeTimers()` or an injected abort signal), API error.
- Do **not** add production code in this item.

## Key Files

- `tests/lib/llm.test.ts`
- `src/lib/search.ts` (interface location — reference only, do not edit here)

## Deliverables

- Red contract test suite pinning `ChatClient.available` and `ChatClient.complete(prompt: string): Promise<string>`.
- The exact interface/constructor signature pinned by these tests is the contract consumed by WL-0MUQ0VOPX0037QS7, WL-0MUQ0VPQ7000TH98 and WL-0MUQ0VQ8A002HHFA.

## Dependencies

None.

## Goal

Add the `interview.intelligent` opt-in configuration flag to the `WorklogConfig` type and config loading/validation, with tests, so the interview command can enable the LLM fallback from `.worklog/config.yaml` as an alternative to the `--llm` flag.

Parent: WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF (interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `WorklogConfig` gains an optional `interview?: { intelligent?: boolean }` section in `packages/shared/src/types.ts`, documented in the interface JSDoc.
- Config loading/validation accepts a valid `interview` section and preserves it; a non-object `interview` value or a non-boolean `intelligent` value produces a clear validation error.
- An absent `interview` section defaults to LLM fallback **off** (no behaviour change for existing users).
- Tests in `tests/unit/config-llm.test.ts` (or a sibling `tests/unit/config-interview.test.ts`) cover: absent section, `intelligent: true`, and each invalid shape.
- Precedence is documented and tested at the resolution boundary: the `--llm` CLI flag (WL-0MUQ0VQ8A002HHFA) takes precedence over `interview.intelligent`; provider settings always come from `llm.*` (`resolveLlmConfig`).
- No existing test regresses.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `WorklogConfig` in `packages/shared/src/types.ts` with the optional `interview` section.
- Add a `validateInterviewConfig()` (or extend the existing config validation switch) and an `isIntelligentInterviewEnabled(config)` resolver helper in `src/config.ts`, mirroring `validateLlmConfig()` / `resolveLlmConfig()`.
- Add unit tests mirroring the structure of `tests/unit/config-llm.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`
- `src/config.ts`
- `tests/unit/config-llm.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Typed, validated and tested `interview.intelligent` config opt-in.

## Dependencies

None.

# a-r (audit reject) should not change work item priority

## Problem statement

The herdr `a-r` ("audit reject") chord silently overwrites the selected work
item's priority with `medium`. Rejecting an item for rework should reset its
lifecycle state (`open` / `plan_complete`) but must preserve the priority the
producer already assigned, so that a `high` or `critical` item is not
downgraded by the act of rejecting it.

## Users

Producers reviewing `in_review` work items in herdr.

- As a producer, when I press `a-r` to reject an item for rework, I want its
  priority to remain unchanged, so that the triage/urgency signal I set is not
  lost.
- As a producer, when I reject a `critical` item, I want it to stay `critical`
  so it re-enters the queue with the correct urgency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `a-r` (audit reject) shortcut command no longer passes `--priority` to
   `wl update`; a rejected item's priority is left unchanged.
2. The `a-r` shortcut still resets the item's `status` to `open` and `stage`
   to `plan_complete`, and still runs `wl reviewed <id> false` and
   `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` with the rejection summary.
3. The `a-r` shortcut label/description no longer claim a priority reset
   (description reads "reset it to open/plan_complete for rework").
4. Shortcut-config, worklist and herdr shortcut tests are updated to assert the
   priority-preserving behaviour; no test asserts the removed `--priority medium`
   token.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Change is confined to the bundled shortcut definition and its test fixtures.
- Backwards compatibility for `wl update --priority <level>` is unaffected; only
  the `a-r` shortcut stops supplying the flag.
- Keep the `a-y` (audit approve) behaviour unchanged — it already does not
  touch priority.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` defines the `a-r` chord as:

```text
!!wl reviewed <id> false && wl update <id> --status open --stage plan_complete --priority medium && wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no --summary 'Rejected by manual review. <reason>'
```

with description "Reject the in_review item and reset it to
open/plan_complete/medium for rework." This was deliberately introduced by the
now-completed work item WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2 ("a-r (audit reject) should reset
item to open/plan_complete/medium"); the priority reset is now considered
undesirable because it destroys the producer's priority signal.

## Desired change

Drop the `--priority medium` token from the `a-r` command chain and update the
shortcut description accordingly, so rejection preserves the item's priority.
Update the affected test fixtures and assertions to match.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Remove `--priority medium` from the `a-r` command; update its `description`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Update the two `a-r` assertions (WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2 tests) to expect no `--priority` token.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Update the `a-r` compound-command fixture/resolved command.
- `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts` — Update the `a-r` fixture and resolved-command expectation.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Confirm no documented claim of a priority reset; adjust if present.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2** — "a-r (audit reject) should reset item to open/plan_complete/medium" (completed). Introduced the `--priority medium` token this item removes; direct predecessor.
- **WL-0MU7KEX65004X0U9** — rejection reasons with apostrophes no longer break the audit reject shortcut (completed). Same chord.
- **WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV** — audit fingerprint repair affecting the `a-y`/`a-r` background shortcuts (completed). Same chord.
- **WL-0MTA217DZ003H5K8** — shortcut commands not refreshing the selection list; listed `a-r` among modifying chords (completed).
- **WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL** — `open_pane: false` background dispatch, used by `a-r`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLX5OADB1TECIZV** – Testing: automation - create work item (completed)
- **WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G** – Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (completed)
- **WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV** – Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: also, audit, change, chord, command, herdr, item, medium, priority, reject, reset, review, rework, running, sets, shortcut, should, stage, status, when, work
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: also, audit, change, command, herdr, item, medium, priority, reject, reset, review, rework, running, sets, should, stage, status, when, work
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: audit, change, chord, command, herdr, item, medium, priority, reject, reset, running, shortcut, should, stage, status, when, work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Intent reversal**: WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2 deliberately added the priority reset.
  Assumption: the producer now wants it removed and treats the reset as
  unintended data loss. Documented as a deliberate reversal.
- **Hidden coupling**: other code or docs may assume rejection resets priority.
  Mitigation: repo-wide search for the command string and `plan_complete/medium`
  before/after the change.
- **Test drift**: fixtures copy the command verbatim in several test files;
  mitigation: update all occurrences in one change and let the full suite
  verify.
- **Scope creep**: e.g. adding "restore previous priority" history. Record any
  such idea as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked. The seed context supplied with the
`/intake` invocation was sufficient to draft the brief:

- **Seed**: "When running a-r the command sets the priority of the work item to
  medium. It should not change the priority."
- **Follow-up** — the operator clarified that `a-r` is the herdr
  "audit - reject" chord (a manual producer-audit rejection shortcut) and that
  the priority must not be changed. Source: interactive reply in this session.
- **Research**: located the concrete defect in
  `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (the `a-r` command passes
  `--priority medium`) and its test fixtures. The behaviour was introduced by
  the completed work item WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2; this intake records a deliberate
  reversal of that specific aspect (priority reset), preserving the rest
  (status/stage reset, `reviewed false`, `audit-set`).
data.title: a-r (audit reject) should not change work item priority
